name: Rumble, Mechanized Menace
howItPlays: You fill the field with Mech units, and Rumble's ability makes every one of them tougher whenever it's defending a battlefield you hold. You keep making more Mechs from several different cards at once until your opponent can't clear them all off the field.
whyYou: You like a deck that does one clear thing well: put units down, hold your ground, and let the numbers add up. You're not looking to memorize a tricky sequence of plays, you just want to know your plan going in and execute it well each game. Rumble suits you if you'd rather build a wide, sturdy field than chase one clever combination, and it's a comfortable deck to learn Riftbound with.
ratingNotes: Ability: your Mechs have Shield, +1 Might while they're defenders (Riftcodex, SFD-181). pace 4.5: riftboundguide describes 'board development and recycling rather than early aggression or rapid finishes,' a grinding plan rather than a fast close. stance 6: both sources call the deck proactive ('play Mechs, hold battlefields, and let the board grow'), though it also leans on Shield to defend rather than only attacking. complexity 4: riftboundguide is explicit that 'there is no sequencing puzzle to solve before you can play' and the plan is 'the same every game'; hextechanalytics rates a fully upgraded competitive build higher for attack/defend/recycle decisions, but the core loop this Legend is best known for, including in its starter product, is simple. variance 3: riftboundguide highlights 'four separate sources of Mech token generation' preventing reliance on any one card, and hextechanalytics calls it 'moderately consistent.' archetype Midrange: sources call it 'aggro-control' and 'tribal/engine-focused,' neither a clean fit; it develops and holds rather than racing, so Midrange fits better than Aggro. starterDeck 'Spiritforged Champion Deck' confirmed: riftboundguide's title ('Champion Deck Guide: What's Inside and Is It Worth Buying?') plus a separate riftmana 'Beginner Guide: Starter Spiritforged Rumble Deck' page both point to this being a real retail product built around Rumble. Confidence: high, two solid guides read, a consistent picture of the deck, and a confirmed starter product.
